about: The evergreen bank for the Day 12 daily brief: 25 true, well-documented good-news stories where AI was the reason something good happened outside the AI industry. Used to fill slots on thin news days. Every fact in a summary was read in the primary source on the checked_on date; journal papers were read as the paper's own abstract and author record on Europe PMC, linked here by DOI. Scores follow docs/scoring.md (mass appeal x3, real person or place x2, stage x2, surprise x1, top mark 24).

stories.title: AI reads eye scans as well as specialists at Moorfields
stories.summary: Researchers from DeepMind, Moorfields Eye Hospital and University College London trained an AI on 14,884 three-dimensional eye scans from patients referred to a major eye hospital. Its recommendations on who needed referring reached or exceeded those of experts across a range of sight-threatening retinal diseases. The study was published in Nature Medicine in August 2018.
stories.confirmed: The Nature Medicine abstract says referral recommendations reached or exceeded experts on a range of sight-threatening retinal diseases after training on only 14,884 scans, and the author record lists DeepMind, Moorfields Eye Hospital and UCL.
stories.line: An AI trained with Moorfields Eye Hospital in London learnt to read eye scans and flag sight-threatening disease as well as the experts.

stories.title: AI-supported breast screening in Sweden finds more cancers with less reading
stories.summary: The MASAI trial in Sweden randomly assigned more than 105,000 women to breast screening read with AI support or to standard double reading by two radiologists. The AI-supported group had higher sensitivity (80.5% against 73.8%), the same specificity, and no more cancers turning up between screenings. An earlier analysis from the same trial found the screen-reading workload fell by 44.3%.
stories.confirmed: The Lancet abstract reports 105,934 women randomised, sensitivity of 80.5% with AI against 73.8% without, specificity of 98.5% in both groups and a non-inferior interval cancer rate; the 2023 Lancet Oncology abstract reports the 44.3% workload reduction.
stories.line: In a Swedish trial of over 100,000 women, breast screening with AI helping the radiologist caught more cancers and nearly halved the work.

stories.title: AI finds halicin, a new kind of antibiotic
stories.summary: A team at MIT trained a deep learning model to predict which molecules kill bacteria and used it to pick out a compound they named halicin. In lab tests it killed many drug-resistant bacteria, and it cleared resistant infections in mice. The work was published in Cell in February 2020; it has not been tested in people.
stories.confirmed: MIT News says the model picked out halicin, which killed many resistant strains in the lab and cleared A. baumannii infections in mice within 24 hours; the Cell abstract says halicin treated C. difficile and pan-resistant A. baumannii infections in mice.
stories.line: MIT scientists used AI to find halicin, a new kind of antibiotic that wiped out stubborn drug-resistant infections in mice.

stories.title: First AI cleared to check for diabetic eye disease without a specialist
stories.summary: A trial in primary care clinics tested an AI system that checks photos of the back of the eye for diabetic retinopathy in 900 people with diabetes. It beat all its pre-set targets, and the US regulator then authorised it as the first autonomous AI diagnostic system in any field of medicine. It gives a result without an eye specialist needing to look at the image.
stories.confirmed: The npj Digital Medicine abstract reports 900 participants at primary care clinics, sensitivity of 87.2% and specificity of 90.7%, and says the FDA authorised it as the first autonomous AI diagnostic system in any field of medicine.
stories.line: People with diabetes in the US get their eyes checked for damage by an AI camera at their local doctor's, with no eye specialist needed.

stories.title: Sepsis early-warning AI linked to fewer deaths at five hospitals
stories.summary: An AI early-warning system for sepsis called TREWS monitored 590,736 patients across five hospitals in a study led by Johns Hopkins. Among 6,877 sepsis patients the system flagged before antibiotics were started, those whose alert was confirmed by a clinician within three hours had a lower death rate, a relative reduction of 18.7%. The study was published in Nature Medicine in July 2022.
stories.confirmed: The Nature Medicine abstract reports 590,736 patients monitored across five hospitals and an 18.7% adjusted relative reduction in in-hospital deaths when alerts were confirmed within three hours; the author record lists Johns Hopkins institutions.
stories.line: At five hospitals in a Johns Hopkins study, an AI that spots sepsis early got doctors to patients sooner, and fewer of them died.

stories.title: AI brain-scan reading in every stroke centre in England
stories.summary: AI tools that read brain scans and flag signs of a major stroke within minutes were rolled out to all stroke centres in England in summer 2024. A study in The Lancet Digital Health found that at the 26 hospitals evaluated, the share of patients getting clot-removing surgery doubled from 2.3% to 4.6%. NHS England also reported transfers to specialist centres happening 64 minutes sooner at primary stroke centres.
stories.confirmed: The NHS England release says the tools were rolled out to all stroke centres in England in summer 2024 and reports the 64-minute reduction; the Lancet Digital Health abstract reports thrombectomy rising from 2.3% to 4.6% at 26 evaluation sites.
stories.line: Every stroke centre in England now has AI reading brain scans in minutes. Where it was studied, twice as many patients had clots removed.

stories.title: AI river flood forecasts running in more than 80 countries
stories.summary: Google researchers showed in Nature that an AI model forecasts extreme river floods five days ahead as reliably as the leading global system manages on the day itself, including on rivers with no measuring gauges. The model runs in a free public warning system covering more than 80 countries. Google says the forecasts reach up to seven days ahead and cover 460 million people.
stories.confirmed: The Nature abstract says five-day AI forecasts are as reliable as or better than same-day forecasts from the current leading system and that the model runs in a free, public early warning system in over 80 countries; Google's post gives the seven days and 460 million people.
stories.line: AI now forecasts river floods up to seven days ahead in more than 80 countries, with free forecasts covering 460 million people.

stories.title: AI-watched cameras spot California wildfires early
stories.summary: ALERTCalifornia, led by UC San Diego, watches the state's highest fire-risk areas around the clock with more than 1,000 cameras. AI scans the feeds for signs of fire and alerts trained staff, who confirm before firefighters respond; it was rolled out to all 21 CAL FIRE units in September 2023. The programme's director said that in 2025 it alerted fire officials before 911 callers did in more than half of about 3,600 incidents.
stories.confirmed: The UC San Diego article says more than 1,050 cameras monitor fire-threat regions 24 hours a day and that the AI went to all 21 CAL FIRE units in September 2023; Route Fifty reports the director's 2025 figures on alerts ahead of 911 callers.
stories.line: Over 1,000 AI-watched cameras scan California for smoke day and night, often tipping off firefighters before anyone has rung 911.

stories.title: Pilots cut planet-warming vapour trails using AI forecasts
stories.summary: In a randomised trial on commercial American Airlines flights, pilots changed altitude to avoid air where forecasts, including one from a machine learning model, said vapour trails would form. Satellite images showed 64% fewer trails on those flights than on comparison flights, for about 2% more fuel on the adjusted flights. The study, by Google Research, American Airlines and Breakthrough Energy, was published in Communications Engineering in December 2024.
stories.confirmed: The Communications Engineering abstract reports a randomised trial on commercial flights with 64% fewer contrails on treatment flights (p = 0.0331) and about 2% more fuel per adjusted flight; the author record lists Google Research, American Airlines and Breakthrough Energy.
stories.line: American Airlines pilots used AI forecasts to steer clear of air that makes planet-warming vapour trails, and cut them by 64% in a trial.

stories.title: AI counts 1.8 billion trees across the West African Sahara and Sahel
stories.summary: Scientists used deep learning on very sharp satellite images to map the crown of every tree across about 1.3 million square kilometres of the West African Sahara, Sahel and neighbouring sub-humid zone. They found more than 1.8 billion individual trees, an unexpectedly large number that challenges the usual story of dryland turning to desert. The study was published in Nature in October 2020.
stories.confirmed: The Nature abstract reports over 1.8 billion individual trees detected with deep learning across about 1.3 million square kilometres of the West African Sahara, Sahel and sub-humid zone, and calls the density surprisingly high.
stories.line: AI counted trees one by one in satellite photos of West Africa's drylands, Sahara included, and found 1.8 billion. Far more than expected.

stories.title: AI finds an eighth planet around a distant star
stories.summary: A Google engineer and a NASA-funded astronomer trained a neural network on 15,000 signals from NASA's Kepler space telescope and used it to search for planets earlier methods had missed. It found Kepler-90i, a hot, rocky world and the eighth planet known around the star Kepler-90. That tied the system with our own for the most known planets around a single star.
stories.confirmed: The NASA release of 14 December 2017 says a neural network trained on 15,000 vetted Kepler signals found Kepler-90i, the eighth planet around Kepler-90, tying it with our solar system for the most planets around one star.
stories.line: AI sifting through old NASA telescope data found an eighth planet around a far-off star, matching our own solar system's tally.

stories.title: AI spots fresh craters on Mars
stories.summary: A machine learning tool built at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory found a cluster of recently formed craters in a region of Mars called Noctis Fossae, the first time AI had found previously unknown craters there. A sharper camera on NASA's Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter confirmed the find in August 2020. A researcher needs about 40 minutes to scan one of the orbiter's images; the tool takes about five seconds.
stories.confirmed: The JPL article of 1 October 2020 says machine learning found a crater cluster in Noctis Fossae, confirmed by the HiRISE camera on 26 August 2020, and that the tool takes about five seconds per image against about 40 minutes for a researcher.
stories.line: A NASA AI spotted fresh craters on Mars from orbit, checking each photo in about five seconds where a scientist needs 40 minutes.

stories.title: Perseverance completes the first AI-planned drives on Mars
stories.summary: On 8 and 10 December 2025, NASA's Perseverance rover drove 210 metres and then 246 metres along the rim of Jezero Crater on routes planned by generative AI instead of human route planners. NASA called them the first drives on another world planned by AI. Engineers checked the commands on a virtual copy of the rover before sending them to Mars.
stories.confirmed: The JPL release of 30 January 2026 says Perseverance completed the first AI-planned drives on another world on 8 and 10 December 2025, covering 210 metres and 246 metres, with commands checked on a digital twin of the rover first.
stories.line: NASA's Perseverance rover drove 456 metres across Mars on routes planned by AI, the first AI-planned drives on another world.

stories.title: Brain implant and AI let a man with ALS speak again
stories.summary: Casey Harrell, a 45-year-old man whose speech had been badly damaged by ALS, had sensors implanted in his brain as part of the BrainGate2 clinical trial at UC Davis Health. Machine learning turns the brain activity of his attempts to speak into words on a screen, read aloud in a voice built to sound like his own before the illness. The system held 97.5% accuracy over more than eight months, according to results in the New England Journal of Medicine.
stories.confirmed: The UC Davis Health release names Casey Harrell, 45, and says the system turns brain signals into speech with up to 97% accuracy in a voice like his own before ALS; the NEJM abstract reports 97.5% accuracy sustained over 8.4 months.
stories.line: Casey Harrell lost his speech to ALS. A brain implant and AI now turn the words he tries to say into speech, in a voice like his old one.

stories.title: AI turns brain signals into speech and a talking avatar
stories.summary: In a clinical trial reported in Nature, researchers recorded brain signals from a participant with severe paralysis who was unable to speak, as the person tried to say sentences silently. Deep learning models turned the signals into text at a median of 78 words a minute, into speech personalised to the participant's voice from before the injury, and into the facial movements of an on-screen avatar.
stories.confirmed: The Nature abstract reports real-time decoding into text at a median of 78 words a minute, speech personalised to the participant's pre-injury voice and facial-avatar animation, in a clinical-trial participant with severe limb and vocal paralysis.
stories.line: Someone left unable to speak by paralysis talked again through an on-screen avatar, as AI turned brain signals into a voice and a face.

stories.title: Be My AI describes the world for blind people
stories.summary: In 2023 the free Be My Eyes app added Be My AI: a blind or low-vision user takes a photo, gets a detailed description and can ask follow-up questions, with human volunteers still on hand. More than 19,000 blind and low-vision people tested it first. In a 2023 survey by a US research centre on blindness, nearly half of Be My Eyes users had tried it and all but one of the 76 who commented were positive, though a few noted it can be inconsistent.
stories.confirmed: The Be My Eyes post of 25 September 2023 describes taking a photo, getting a detailed description and asking follow-up questions, with over 19,000 blind and low-vision beta testers; the AccessWorld article reports the survey figures.
stories.line: Blind people now point a phone at anything and a free app's AI describes it in detail, then answers whatever they ask next.

stories.title: AI rebuilds Sarah Ezekiel's voice from seconds of old video
stories.summary: Sarah Ezekiel, an artist from London, was diagnosed with motor neurone disease in 2000 and lost her speech. Assistive technology company Smartbox and ElevenLabs used AI to recreate her voice from a single line of speech in an old home video, a clip reported as eight seconds long. Her children heard her speak in a natural voice, cockney accent included, for the first time, and she said she almost cried when she first heard it.
stories.confirmed: The Smartbox page says Sarah Ezekiel was diagnosed with MND in April 2000 and that ElevenLabs recreated her voice with AI from a single line of speech in an old video; NR Times reports the eight-second VHS clip and the cockney accent.
stories.line: Sarah Ezekiel lost her voice to motor neurone disease in 2000. AI rebuilt it from a few seconds of old home video, cockney accent and all.

stories.title: AlphaFold works out the shapes of proteins
stories.summary: Working out a protein's shape from its building blocks had been an open problem for more than 50 years. In 2021 the AlphaFold team published in Nature the first method to regularly predict protein shapes with atomic accuracy. It has since been used to predict the structure of virtually all 200 million known proteins, more than two million people in 190 countries have used it, and its creators shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
stories.confirmed: The Nature abstract describes the first computational method to regularly predict protein structures with atomic accuracy, a problem open for over 50 years; the Utrecht University page reports the Nobel Prize, the 200 million proteins and two million users in 190 countries.
stories.line: AlphaFold cracked a 50-year-old puzzle about the building blocks of life. Two million scientists now use it, and it won a Nobel Prize.

stories.title: AI helps find 303 new Nazca figures in six months
stories.summary: It took nearly a century to find 430 of the ancient figures drawn into the ground at Nazca in Peru. A team led by Yamagata University used AI to search the whole region and found 303 more in six months of fieldwork, nearly doubling the known total. The results were published in PNAS in September 2024.
stories.confirmed: The PNAS abstract says it took nearly a century to discover 430 figurative Nazca geoglyphs and that an AI system led to the discovery of 303 new ones within six months of field survey, nearly doubling the number known.
stories.line: AI helped archaeologists find 303 new ancient drawings in Peru's Nazca desert in six months, nearly doubling a century of discoveries.

stories.title: Students use AI to read a scroll charred by Vesuvius
stories.summary: Three students, Youssef Nader, Luke Farritor and Julian Schilliger, won the $700,000 Vesuvius Challenge grand prize in February 2024 for reading a rolled-up scroll from Herculaneum that was charred when Vesuvius erupted about 2,000 years ago. Machine learning picked out ink in X-ray scans, revealing more than 2,000 characters across 15 columns of Greek. The text is a previously unknown work of philosophy about pleasure, touching on music and food, and a team of papyrologists reviewed the result.
stories.confirmed: The Vesuvius Challenge page announces the $700,000 grand prize on 5 February 2024 to Nader, Farritor and Schilliger for 15 columns and more than 2,000 characters, reviewed by papyrologists; the Nature report reprinted by Scientific American confirms the winners and the subject.
stories.line: Three students used AI to read a scroll burnt shut by Vesuvius 2,000 years ago. Inside, a philosopher musing on pleasure, music and food.

stories.title: AI helps show that elephants call each other by name
stories.summary: Researchers used machine learning on the calls of wild African elephants and showed that the elephant a call was meant for can be predicted from the sound of the call itself. When calls were played back, elephants responded more to calls originally addressed to them than to calls meant for another elephant. The study was published in Nature Ecology and Evolution in June 2024.
stories.confirmed: The Nature Ecology and Evolution abstract says wild African elephants address one another with individually specific calls, that machine learning predicted the receiver from a call's structure, and that elephants responded differently to calls addressed to them.
stories.line: Scientists ran AI over the rumbles of wild African elephants and found they call each other by something very like names.

stories.title: Europe's weather centre switches on an AI forecast
stories.summary: On 25 February 2025 the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts made its AI forecasting system, the AIFS, fully operational, running alongside its traditional physics-based model. The centre says it outperforms state-of-the-art physics-based models on many measures, including the tracks of tropical cyclones, with gains of up to 20%. It uses roughly 1,000 times less energy to produce a forecast.
stories.confirmed: The ECMWF news item of 25 February 2025 says the AIFS became operational alongside the physics-based system, outperforms state-of-the-art physics-based models for many measures with gains of up to 20%, and uses roughly 1,000 times less energy per forecast.
stories.line: Europe's weather centre now runs an AI forecast every day. It beats the old method on many measures and uses about 1,000 times less energy.

stories.title: AI monsoon forecasts reach 38 million farmers in India
stories.summary: In summer 2025 India's Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare sent AI-based monsoon forecasts by text message to about 38 million farmers, up to four weeks before the rains arrived. The forecasts, built with teams at the University of Chicago and UC Berkeley, correctly predicted that the monsoon would stall for about three weeks after an early start. Odisha's state government reached nearly a million more farmers by voice message.
stories.confirmed: The University of Chicago article of 15 September 2025 says the ministry sent AI-based forecasts by SMS to 38 million farmers up to four weeks ahead and that the forecast predicted the monsoon's stall; the UC Berkeley article gives the same figures.
stories.line: 38 million farmers in India got AI monsoon forecasts by text up to four weeks ahead, including a heads-up that the rains would stall.

stories.title: Merlin tells you which bird is singing
stories.summary: In June 2021 the Cornell Lab of Ornithology added Sound ID to its free Merlin Bird ID app. The phone listens and shows a live list, with photos, of the birds singing nearby, even when several sing at once. It works by turning sound into pictures and using image-recognition AI trained on thousands of recordings shared by birdwatchers, and it launched with more than 400 species from the US and Canada.
stories.confirmed: The Cornell Chronicle article of 23 June 2021 says Sound ID in the free Merlin app identifies more than 400 US and Canadian species by song in real time, using image classification on spectrograms of recordings contributed through eBird.
stories.line: Hold up your phone and Cornell's free Merlin app listens to the birdsong and tells you who's singing, taught by birdwatchers' recordings.

stories.title: Students learn more in less time with an AI tutor in a Harvard trial
stories.summary: In a randomised controlled trial in a Harvard physics course, students learnt material either through a specially designed AI tutor or in an active-learning class built on the same teaching principles. Those using the AI tutor learnt significantly more in less time, and felt more engaged and motivated. The trial was published in Scientific Reports in June 2025; it covered one course and tested learning in the short term.
stories.confirmed: The Scientific Reports abstract describes a randomised controlled trial in which college students learnt significantly more in less time with the AI tutor than in an active-learning class, and felt more engaged and more motivated.
stories.line: In a Harvard physics trial, students with a carefully built AI tutor learnt more in less time than in a good class, and felt more engaged.
